title: Latent Riemannian Flow Matching for Geometry-Grounded 3D Foundation Models
claim: Frozen foundation-model latents can be generated by flow matching on their native manifold, then decoded into consistent 3D outputs.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right flow, spheres mid-figure, 3D scene output at right
description: A single wide left-to-right pipeline diagram. At left, four input photos of an office (labelled 'Input multi-view') feed a frozen VGGT block (snowflake icon) that outputs small colored token squares per view. Those tokens, along with noise patches and a camera icon for the target pose, enter a trainable flow model v_w (flame icon). Its output tokens go to a column of four colored bars, each tied to a sphere ('Product Manifold') with a red tangent arrow and a blue trajectory curve. The sphere outputs merge into one token stack that feeds a frozen DPT head and a trainable ViT head. These produce PM and RGB outputs. At right is a large point-cloud render of the generated room ('Novel Scan Generation'), where the eye lands last.
caption: Method overview. Given a sparse set of unposed RGB observations, a frozen VGGT encoder extracts per-view latent tokens. A learned Riemannian flow matching model vw generates latent codes conditioned on the tokens of the input views and a target camera pose, operating directly on the product manifold of four zero-mean hyperspheres. Frozen DPT decoding heads reconstruct point maps (PM) from the generated latents, while a trained RGB decoder produces full photometric reconstructions, enabling novel scan generation of complete, geometrically consistent 3D scenes.
abstract: Geometric foundation models such as the Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) provide strong 3D priors from unposed images, but operate deterministically and cannot generate plausible geometry beyond what the observations directly support. We bridge geometric foundation models and generative 3D modeling by performing flow matching directly in their latent space, leveraging learned 3D priors without committing to explicit representations such as Gaussians, meshes, or video-VAE latents. This requires respecting the latent geometry: LayerNorm places the decoder inputs on a product of zero-mean hyperspheres, and treating this space as unconstrained Euclidean substantially degrades flow matching. We therefore formulate Riemannian flow matching on this product manifold, conditioned on unposed context views and a target camera pose, keeping generated tokens within the geometry expected by the frozen decoder. Our main experiments use VGGT, while additional experiments with Depth Anything 3 show that the same formulation transfers to a different independently pretrained 3D backbone without modification. On RealEstate10K, ScanNet++, and ETH3D, our method achieves strong results against recent scene-generation baselines in both novel-view appearance and aggregated 3D geometry, establishing latent-space flow matching on geometric foundation models as a viable paradigm for 3D generation.
